title: Civilian-agency FISMA effectiveness: Fiscal Year 2022
summary: Inspectors general rated 15 of 23 reviewed civilian-agency information-security programs ineffective for FY 2022. GAO called for measures better linked to goals, risk, workforce, and agency size.
key_findings: Inspectors general rated 15 of 23 reviewed civilian-agency information-security programs ineffective for FY 2022.
Method: GAO review of agency self-assessments, inspector-general determinations, and federal FISMA metrics.
Attribution: Inspector-general assessments synthesized by GAO.
why_it_matters: This observation adds one of three time points for the civilian-agency fisma effectiveness series and keeps its unit, denominator, period, geography, method, attribution, and series-break context attached.
ftfn_relevance: Adds one of twelve Phase 56A primary records for institutional AI and cybersecurity system performance.
Supports a within-domain time series without creating a cross-domain score.
Makes revision, denominator, and method limits visible before a direction is described.
evidence_limits: GAO called for measures better linked to goals, risk, workforce, and agency size.
The observation is bounded to United States federal government and the stated period.
The denominator is Twenty-three civilian executive-branch agencies.
Two-point movement is not presented as a durable trend without an explicit caveat.
